Figure 1:Exampled future 4D world generated byPlan4D.Given an observed scene context and a text-specified action,Plan4Dgenerates a future video together with synchronized depth, camera rays, and scene flow (subset shown), which are further lifted into a dynamic 4D scene.
Top: fine-grained hand-object interaction.
Bottom: camera motion with scene-level geometry changes.

Figure 2:Overview of thePlan4Dpipeline.A video generator produces a denoised latent trajectory, while a stitched DA3 decoder reads the same latent state to recover synchronized depth, camera rays, camera parameters, point clouds, and scene flow.
During joint training, the stitched decoder is frozen and acts as a differentiable geometry critic for the video generator; at inference time, RGB video and dense 4D structure are decoded from the shared latent trajectory.

Figure 3:Qualitative results for scene flow and dynamic reconstruction.Columns from left to right compare the ground truth, results from our DA3-based prediction, Any4D, and MotionCrafter.
Our result better preserves object-level motion and dynamic 3D structure while maintaining consistency with the reference geometry.
Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on ETH3D (top) and ScanNet++ (bottom).Our stitched decoder preserves DA3-like surface layout and scene structure more faithfully than the other aligned decoders.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison betweenPlan4Dand TesserAct[117]for action-conditioned RGB-D world generation.The input consists of the first RGB frame and the action text:Hold the small glass dish. Dispense pink liquid using a pipette. Release the liquid smoothly. Fill the dish gradually.. The first two rows show our results, and the lower rows show TesserAct.

Figure 6:Qualitative comparison betweenPlan4Dand Gen3R[37]for dynamic 4D world generation.The middle panels show the global dynamic point-cloud reconstruction, and the right panels show the corresponding RGB frames.

Figure 8:Stitching adapter architecture ablation over DA3 encoder blocks 1–11. Lower MSE means that the adapter reconstructs the frozen DA3 feature grid more accurately from the Wan VAE latent. All three variants prefer the earliest candidate block, and the linear 3D convolution remains close to the heavier residual and attention-based adapters across the sweep.

Case (a) illustrates a scene transition (C) under Type A. Cases (b) and (c) illustrate object and scene transformations (M) under Type B.
